title: Redo the effort story under the test-focus guidance

intentCoverage.report:
**Assertion gap**, bounded to one maintained boundary consumer. The check exercised the common boundary preparation path and passed while that path unnecessarily requested and completed an app build. This finding covers the selected consumer, not the entire suite.

Story: `SEED-391#redo-the-effort-story-under-the-test-focus-guidance`, completed revision `fbfaa116b961a445cc606fd05363bf75f6ecad5f`. Intent comes from `.planning/seeds/SEED-391-check-test-focus-guidance-by-redoing-a-story.md`, plan 668 slice 2, and its `ci-repair.md`: boundary-only workers prepare the server bundle and request no app.

Target selection changed consequentially from the broad research outcome to that mandatory CI correction's executable promise. I chose `dashboard/backend-tests/review/story-review-state-admission.spec.ts:22`, whose file-level `serverMode: "boundary"` and inherited dashboard fixture actually request `dashboardServerInputsReady`. The previously recorded `runtime/boundary-server.spec.ts` directly starts its server and bypasses this readiness dependency; using it alone would leave the selected fault unreached. The chosen check is nearest relevant proof, and its existing review-state assertions remain intact.

The single temporary fault was in `dashboard/tests/support/pageTest.ts:76`: replace `...(serverMode === "preview" ? [app.dashboardAppArtifactKey] : [])` with unconditional `app.dashboardAppArtifactKey`. Only this infrastructure expression changed. No scenario, fixture data, assertion, timeout or synchronization changed. Test-entry selection resolved MakeMe true and pageObjects false for the selected backend spec; the MakeMe convention was read.

An independent clone at `/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-391-boundary-fbfaa116b/checkout` started clean at the exact revision. Node 24.21.0, the checkout's locked native npm setup, and native Chromium validation passed. AC power was observed before and after proof. Natural one-minute load was 3.85 before baseline, 3.58 after baseline and 4.76 after the sequence; no synthetic load was added. Each run used `caffeinate -s -i`, two requested workers and the unchanged default case budget; the single selected case used one worker. No paid native-host run occurred. The scratch revision's `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/references/failure-policy.md` applied throughout.

All three runs used the same maintained command:

```sh
npm run test:dashboard:backend -- dashboard/backend-tests/review/story-review-state-admission.spec.ts --grep 'a review state request for an unconfigured project' --workers=2 --reporter=line
```

Only the external artifact-trace output filename changed between runs. Baseline: 1/1 passed in 4.2 seconds, zero app requests. Fault: 1/1 passed in 3.4 seconds. The existing `OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_ARTIFACT_TRACE` independently recorded an `app` request and start at epoch 1794885470897 ms, then completion at 1794885472890 ms: a real 1.993-second app build on this boundary-only path. Every phase recorded two server-bundle requests. The selected assertions still verified rejected requests, unchanged review state and the empty saved-state answer, but none observed unnecessary app preparation. This establishes wrong behavior on the exercised path, beyond merely executing the changed expression.

An EXIT/signal restoration trap was installed before mutation. After restoration, the identical command passed 1/1 in 1.4 seconds with zero app requests. Byte comparison matched the saved pre-probe infrastructure file; the spec matched its exact revision bytes; `git diff --exit-code` passed and final status was empty. All trace-recorded temporary artifact directories had been removed by run teardown, and no scratch test process remained in the process inspection. Scratch logs, three artifact traces, `fault.patch`, and the clean restored checkout remain under `/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-391-boundary-fbfaa116b/` for caller inspection and disposal. Nothing was written in the shared checkout, committed or pushed.

Next proof action: add an observing assertion at the common preparation owner's focused infrastructure proof that a boundary dashboard requests the server bundle and zero app artifacts. Preserve the product consumer's current scenario assertions. The caller owns repair selection and routing.

Prior disposition: this matches the accepted no-app requirement and earlier manual artifact-trace observation in `ci-repair.md`. The restored revision satisfies the observed promise.
